pitch-law.description: D-STAR pitch law: decoded pitch matches DVSI, quality improves, level and band balance hold, other modes untouched.

shelf.description: High-band shelf re-tuned toward DVSI: 2-4 kHz error to DVSI falls; level, low bands, clipping and quality hold.

tones.description: Tone frames match DVSI's decoder on steady windows; speech PCM is unchanged.

low-band.description: Low-frequency roll-off matched to DVSI's decoders: closer to DVSI's output, nothing else regresses.

encoder.description: D-STAR encoder changes: our encoding, decoded by this library, gets closer to the input without hurting pitch, voicing or level; the decoder is untouched.

encoder-level.description: D-STAR encoder level handling: our encoding keeps the input level as DVSI's encoder does (both decoded by this library) without hurting spectral fit, pitch or voicing; the decoder is untouched.

ambe2450-imbe-encoders.description: AMBE+2 and IMBE encoders: our encoding, decoded by this library, keeps DVSI's level, fits the input at least as well as DVSI's own encoding, stays on pitch and voices like DVSI, sends no tone frames for speech, and clips no more than a few samples where the input itself reaches the rails (t03, t04); the decoders and the D-STAR encoder are untouched (D-STAR's encoded bits identical, so the baseline must record encoder-row hashes).

ambe2450-encoder-tones.description: AMBE+2 encoder tone frames: the tone indices and levels DVSI's encoder sends for its tone vectors, and few tone frames where DVSI sends voice.

dstar-encoder-tones.description: D-STAR encoder tone frames: the tone indices and volumes DVSI's encoder sends for its D-STAR tone vectors, and few tone frames where DVSI sends voice (KNOX tones among them); the AMBE+2 encoder's tone frames and both decoders' tone output unchanged.

call-progress-timing.description: Call-progress tones sent once they fill three spans and held two frames after, as DVSI's encoders send them: no vector gets many tone frames where DVSI sends voice (the 40-45 ms bursts of cpvbad got 45 frames), agreement with DVSI's tone frames does not fall, levels hold, and both decoders' tone output is unchanged.

tone-edges.description: DTMF, KNOX and single tones sent for the frames whose span they fill at least 45% wherever they start within the detector's blocks, and where one changes directly to another, the frame holding both carrying the newer tone if it is a DTMF or KNOX tone filling the span's newest half, else the older if it fills the oldest half, as DVSI's encoders send them: agreement with DVSI's tone frames rises in both encoders, tone frames where DVSI sends voice stay rare, levels hold, and both decoders' tone output is unchanged.

dvsi-parity-development.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-validation.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-final.description: DVSI parity (D-STAR absolute gain and shelf; rate-33 bit layout, pitch law and error counts; output high-pass phase; voiced and unvoiced render gains): our decode of DVSI's bits is no further from DVSI's decoder, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' output, decoded by one decoder, is no further from DVSI's encoding.

dvsi-parity-tones.description: DVSI parity: no tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder, plays a wrong tone more often, or has its encoder tone frames agree less often with DVSI's.

dvsi-parity-channel.description: DVSI parity under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): at no error rate do our mute decisions agree less often with DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

dstar-lost-frames.description: D-STAR b0 125..127 decode as lost frames and the encoder stops sending b0 124/125: DVSI's speech bits decode unchanged, and our encoding loses nothing against the input when both encodings are decoded by a decoder that plays b0 125 as voice (the decoder before this change), so both runs score the same frames.

dstar-repeat-limit-mute.description: D-STAR's repeat-limit mute fades out, keeps the prediction history and mutes at DVSI's level: DVSI's clean speech bits, which never reach the repeat limit, decode unchanged in every mode.

dstar-c0-uncorrectable-channel.description: D-STAR hard decisions play a frame with an uncorrectable C0 word as a lost frame that still predicts the next frame, and repeat no frame on its corrected-error count (#155): under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors) our D-STAR mute decisions agree no less often with DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, and on the loud frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our D-STAR output is no further from DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions.

dstar-c0-uncorrectable-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's error-free speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

dstar-error-level-mute-channel.description: D-STAR hard decisions mute on an error level that counts parity bits and integrates slowly (0.99 level + corrected bits, above 342; #155): under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors) our D-STAR mute decisions agree no less often with DVSI's for hard or soft decisions; their mean over the four hard-decision vectors is at least 0.9975 (with the 1-5% vectors in full agreement, 0.99 at 10%); and on the loud frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our D-STAR output is on average no further from DVSI's, for hard or soft decisions, by more than 0.01 dB.

dstar-error-level-mute-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's error-free speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

dstar-tone-volume-fade-tones.description: A D-STAR tone that goes on at another volume moves to it over the first 80 samples before clipping (#155): on DVSI's tone vectors no steady-tone window of ours agrees less often with DVSI's, plays a wrong tone more often, or is further from DVSI's level, frequency or balance (the frames where the volume changes are scored outside the scoreboard).

dstar-tone-volume-fade-speech.description: The same change leaves DVSI's speech bits decoding unchanged in every mode.

voiced-amplitude-development.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-validation.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-final.description: Voiced amplitude (every harmonic interpolated at steady pitch, its fourth root moving linearly, as on DVSI's AMBE-3000): in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes closer to DVSI's decoder by at least 0.1 dB of log-spectral distance, its envelope correlation with DVSI's and its distance from the input get no worse, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and the encoders' bits are unchanged.

voiced-amplitude-channel.description: Voiced amplitude under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-amplitude-tones.description: Voiced amplitude on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often.

noise-voicing-development.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-validation.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-final.description: Voicing over background noise (#149): at low pitches, where noise passes the voicing test, a 500 Hz column holding little more than the learned background noise (steady mains hum included) is not voiced; magnitudes are unchanged. In every mode our encoding voices like DVSI's more often and voices fewer of DVSI's unvoiced frames, loses no voiced frames or bands (at most 1% of DVSI's voiced frames and 2% of its voiced 1 kHz bands on any vector; of its voiced frames below 80 Hz, 2% on average and 15% on any vector, which hold few), stays as close to DVSI's encoding in spectrum, envelope and level, keeps its pitch, clips no more on any vector, and the decoders are untouched.

noise-voicing-tones.description: Voicing over background noise on DVSI's tone vectors: on no vector do the encoders' tone frames agree less often with DVSI's or add tone frames where DVSI sends voice.

voiced-phase-development.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-validation.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-final.description: Voiced phase (DVSI's onset restart and pitch-switch timing) and rate-33 V/UV rendering, final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's decoder waveform by at least 0.3 more, comes no further from it in log-spectral distance or envelope correlation, no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB; the D-STAR and IMBE encoders' bits are unchanged and the rate-33 encoder's decode is no further from DVSI's encoding.

voiced-phase-channel.description: Voiced phase under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-phase-tones.description: Voiced phase on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

amplitude-limit-development.description: Amplitude limit (no eq 116 scaling on the IMBE and rate-33 paths, as DVSI's decoders), development vectors: P25 and rate 33 come no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance, envelope or waveform correlation and no further from the input than 0.02 dB, their level moves by at most 0.2 dB; D-STAR's PCM and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

amplitude-limit-validation.description: Amplitude limit (no eq 116 scaling on the IMBE and rate-33 paths, as DVSI's decoders), validation vectors: P25 and rate 33 come no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance, envelope or waveform correlation and no further from the input than 0.02 dB, their level moves by at most 0.2 dB; D-STAR's PCM and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

amplitude-limit-channel.description: Amplitude limit under channel errors: in every mode mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

amplitude-limit-tones.description: Amplitude limit on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often.

unvoiced-subframes-development.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-validation.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-final.description: Unvoiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (DVSI's noise sequence, 10 ms subframes under square-root triangular windows, a mid-frame subframe between the two frames' models), final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits comes at least 0.5 dB closer to DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and no further on any vector, correlates with its waveform sample against sample at least 0.005 more, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

unvoiced-subframes-channel.description: Unvoiced synthesis under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

unvoiced-subframes-tones.description: Unvoiced synthesis on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

voiced-subframes-development.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), development vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-validation.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), validation vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-final.description: Voiced synthesis as DVSI's decoders render it (two 10 ms subframes per frame, pitch pulses playing each model's response, and the frame marks that start and end voiced runs), final vectors: in every mode our decode of DVSI's bits correlates with DVSI's waveform sample against sample at least 0.03 more, comes no further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance and by at most 0.05 dB on any vector, keeps its envelope correlation, comes no further from the input than 0.02 dB, its level moves by at most 0.1 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

voiced-subframes-channel.description: Voiced synthesis in subframes under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's as often as before at every error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's.

voiced-subframes-tones.description: Voiced synthesis in subframes on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector's tone output agrees less often with DVSI's decoder or plays a wrong tone more often, and the encoders' tone frames agree with DVSI's as often as before.

ambe2450-tone-fade-tones.description: Rate-33 tones crossfaded with the frames around them over 80 samples, as DVSI's decoder plays them: no rate-33 tone vector's tone level, frequency or twist moves further from DVSI's decoder, none agrees less often with its tone output or plays a wrong tone more often, and no D-STAR tone vector changes in any of these.

ambe2450-tone-fade-speech.description: Rate-33 tone crossfades: the speech vectors hold no tone frame, so every mode's decode of them is unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-development.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), development vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-validation.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), validation vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-final.description: Rate-33 frame handling as DVSI's decoder plays it (silence frames 13.8 dB lower on 15 bands, mutes that fade the last frame out under DVSI's noise level, the frame after a mute or a tone starting afresh, tone 255 and lost frames around tones), final vectors: no mode's decode of the speech vectors changes and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

ambe2450-frames-tones.description: Rate-33 frame handling on the tone vectors: no D-STAR tone vector changes in tone level, frequency, twist, detector agreement or wrong tones, and no rate-33 tone vector agrees less often with DVSI's decoder's tone output, plays a wrong tone more often, or moves its tone frequency or twist further from DVSI's, or its level by more than 0.05 dB.

ambe2450-frames-channel.description: Rate-33 frame handling under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often at any error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB.

pcm-rounding-development.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, development vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-validation.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, validation vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-final.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, final vectors: P25's decode is unchanged; on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector does our decode come further from DVSI's decoder in log-spectral distance by more than 0.01 dB or correlate with DVSI's waveform sample against sample less by more than 0.001, no vector's level moves by more than 0.05 dB, and every encoder's bits are unchanged.

pcm-rounding-tones.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, on the tone vectors: no D-STAR or rate-33 tone vector agrees less often with DVSI's decoder's tone output, plays a wrong tone more often, or moves its tone frequency or twist further from DVSI's, or its level by more than 0.05 dB.

pcm-rounding-channel.description: D-STAR and rate-33 16-bit output rounded to nearest, as DVSI's decoders round it, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): in every mode our mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often at any error rate, hard or soft, and on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) our hard-decision output is no further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB.

unvoiced-code-development.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec (D-STAR b0 123, rate 33 b0 119, P25 b0 127), its amplitudes measured on that code's harmonic grid, development vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, and for each encoder the log-spectral distance of its decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB and its level gap to DVSI's encoding by no more than 0.1 dB.

unvoiced-code-validation.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec (D-STAR b0 123, rate 33 b0 119, P25 b0 127), its amplitudes measured on that code's harmonic grid, validation vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, and for each encoder the log-spectral distance of its decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB and its level gap to DVSI's encoding by no more than 0.1 dB.

unvoiced-code-tones.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec, on the tone vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged (no tone vector moves in detector agreement, wrong tones, tone level, frequency or twist in any mode), and on no D-STAR or rate-33 vector do the encoder's tone frames agree less often with DVSI's or appear where DVSI sends voice more often.

unvoiced-code-channel.description: A voice frame with no voiced band coded at one fixed pitch code per codec, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, so in every mode the mute decisions agree with DVSI's exactly as before at every error rate, hard and soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) is as far from DVSI's as before.

joint-search-development.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, development vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and for the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders the log-spectral distance of the decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB, its envelope correlation with the input falls by no more than 0.002, and its level gap to DVSI's encoding grows by no more than 0.1 dB.

joint-search-validation.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, validation vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, the IMBE encoder's bits are unchanged, and for the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders the log-spectral distance of the decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.01 dB, its envelope correlation with the input falls by no more than 0.002, and its level gap to DVSI's encoding grows by no more than 0.1 dB.

joint-search-tones.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, on the tone vectors: every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged (no tone vector moves in detector agreement, wrong tones, tone level, frequency or twist in any mode), and the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' tone results are unchanged on every vector (agreement with DVSI's tone frames, tone frames where DVSI sends voice, and the level of the tone frames both send).

joint-search-channel.description: The D-STAR and AMBE+2 (rate-33) encoders refine their six spectral vector indices (b3..b8) together after the nearest-row search, two passes minimising the decoder's mean-removed residual error weighted by the square root of each harmonic's amplitude relative to the frame's geometric mean (bounded 0.1..10), and their magnitude scales are recalibrated, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): every decode of DVSI's bits is unchanged, so in every mode the mute decisions agree with DVSI's exactly as before at every error rate, hard and soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) is as far from DVSI's as before.

r33-row-grid-development.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, development vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, every encoder's bits are unchanged, and for rate 33 the log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode falls (mean, 95% interval below 0), the sample-for-sample waveform correlation and the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode fall by no more than 0.0005, the level against DVSI's moves by at most 0.05 dB (mean and every vector), and the log-spectral distance from the input rises by no more than 0.005 dB.

r33-row-grid-validation.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, validation vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, every encoder's bits are unchanged, and for rate 33 the log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode falls (mean, 95% interval below 0), the sample-for-sample waveform correlation and the envelope correlation with DVSI's decode fall by no more than 0.0005, the level against DVSI's moves by at most 0.05 dB (mean and every vector), and the log-spectral distance from the input rises by no more than 0.005 dB.

r33-row-grid-tones.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, on the tone vectors: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged, the D-STAR and rate-33 encoders' tone results are unchanged on every vector, and on no rate-33 vector does our decode agree less often with DVSI's tone output or play a wrong tone more often, or move its tone level or twist further from DVSI's by more than 0.01 dB or its tone frequency by more than 1e-4 relative. Tone frames decode as before; only a speech frame of these rows played under a tone's 80-sample fade-in can move a tone metric, by far less than these tolerances.

r33-row-grid-channel.description: Rate-33 voice frames of V/UV rows 18 to 31 decode on a band grid whose L bands span 3.58 kHz (w0 = 2.81 / L, L from the pitch code, the unvoiced factor from that w0), as the published AMBE-3000R measurement gives and DVSI's decoder plays them, under channel errors (dam at 1.1-10.6% bit errors): the D-STAR and P25 decodes are unchanged (mute decisions and output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes, hard and soft), and for rate 33 the mute decisions agree with DVSI's no less often on any vector, hard or soft, and the output on the frames neither run nor DVSI mutes (at least a tenth of those DVSI plays) comes no further from DVSI's, hard or soft.

encoder-quality-final.description: The three changes of this change set together (the encoders' fixed pitch code for frames with no voiced band, the AMBE encoders' joint choice of their six spectral vectors with recalibrated magnitude scales, and rate-33 V/UV rows 18 to 31 on the published band grid), main against the change set, final vectors. Built from the development and validation gate sets of the three changes (unvoiced-code-*, joint-search-*, r33-row-grid-*) with the same metrics and rules: where two changes bound the same metric their limits are added, and 'unchanged' is kept only where it holds for the change set as a whole. So: the D-STAR and P25 decodes of DVSI's bits are unchanged; for each encoder the log-spectral distance of its decoded encoding from DVSI's encoding and from the input rises by no more than 0.02 dB (D-STAR, rate 33: 0.01 from each encoder change) or 0.01 dB (P25: the first change only) and its level gap to DVSI's encoding grows by no more than 0.2 dB (D-STAR, rate 33) or 0.1 dB (P25); the D-STAR and rate-33 encodings' envelope correlation with the input falls by no more than 0.002 (the second change only); the encoders' bits change, so no bit-identity check is kept; and rate 33's decode, which the third change moves, takes that change's checks: its log-spectral distance from DVSI's decode falls (mean, 95% interval below 0), its sample-for-sample waveform correlation and envelope correlation with DVSI's decode fall by no more than 0.0005, its level against DVSI's moves by at most 0.05 dB (mean and every vector), and its log-spectral distance from the input rises by no more than 0.005 dB.
